edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: Ethanol is metabolized to acetaldehyde, which can damage DNA and proteins, and even lower-dose drinking can raise circulating estradiol and impair folate handling. Those pathways are most relevant to long-latency outcomes like Hepatocellular carcinoma, where cumulative exposure matters more than a single episode.
edges.summary: Heavy alcohol intake appears tied to higher risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in general adult mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Absolute risk changes at low intake are small and can be outweighed by baseline cancer risk, but the linearity of the alcohol signal means 'light' does not mean zero biological effect.
